car.subject: 3522 repack lot #’s do not match original lot #’s.
car.nonconformityDescription: During warehouse inspection, it was identified that the ink lot number printed directly on each bag was correct. However, the four (4) labels applied to the exterior stretch wrap was mislabelled with the incorrect lot number.
car.trueRootCause: The incorrect exterior stretch wrap labels resulted from insufficient staffing during a campaign change and non-routine repacks. Operators were required to manage multiple concurrent operational tasks, reducing the level of oversight available for label verification. The staffing plan did not account for the additional workload associated with repack activities during campaign changeovers, allowing the labeling error to occur.

actions.action:
1. Establish a minimum staffing requirement for all repack activities performed during campaign changeovers. - COMPLETE

2. Assign a minimum of two (2) LCY operators and two (2) Mundy operators whenever repacks are conducted during campaign changes to ensure adequate coverage for all operational and verification activities. - COMPLETE/ON-GOING

3. Reinforce label verification requirements with operations personnel to ensure all exterior stretch-wrap labels are verified against the approved lot number prior to product release. - COMPLETE

5. Monitor implementation of the revised staffing plan during future campaign changeovers to confirm effectiveness and prevent recurrence. - COMPLETE

car.subject: C-Grade Lot Blending 3411U and 3412 Lot 0
car.nonconformityDescription: Two C Grade products were blended together rather than an A grade product with 20-25% C grade.
car.immediateActions: Product was graded as C grade and returned to the grind list for controlled blending at 20% into A-grade product.
car.investigationSummary: Based on the CAR information available, lots 3411U and 3412 Lot 0 were both C grade and were blended together. The required method was to blend A-grade product with only 20–25% C-grade material. The resulting blend tested C grade. The affected product was regraded as C grade and returned to the grind list for controlled 20% use. Batch records, operator instructions, lot-selection/authorization records, and equipment/work-order information still require review.
car.trueRootCause: Preliminary systemic cause — pending record and interview verification: the blend selection and release controls did not require documented verification that one component was A grade and that C-grade content remained within the approved 20–25% range before blending.

whySteps.what: Two C-grade lots were blended together instead of blending A grade with 20–25% C grade.
whySteps.why: Both selected lots were C grade.
whySteps.countermeasure: Review recent blend records and contain any similar mixed-grade combinations.

whySteps.why: The material grade and approved blend ratio were not verified before the blend was charged.
whySteps.countermeasure: Revise the blend/grind instruction and batch record to require verification.

whySteps.why: The current blend selection/release process did not require documented independent verification.
whySteps.countermeasure: Add independent pre-charge signoff for C-grade additions.

whySteps.why: The work instruction and batch record lacked a mandatory control for grade, lot, and ratio confirmation before blending.
whySteps.rootCause: Preliminary root cause: inadequate documented method control for pre-blend grade/lot/ratio verification; confirm through record review and interviews.
whySteps.countermeasure: Train operators and retain competency records.

car.similarNonconformities: The same failure mode could occur in other blend or regrind activities where material grade, lot identity, and blend ratio are selected without a documented pre-charge verification. Review recent applicable blend records and current instructions to determine whether any similar combinations occurred and whether controls are consistently applied.
car.proceduresRevised: Required — blend/grind work instruction and batch record
car.supportingDocuments: Revised instruction, controlled batch record/signoff, training records, and blend-record review log
car.successCriteria: Effectiveness will be demonstrated when 100% of the next 10 applicable blends, monitored for at least 30 days, show correct grade and lot selection, C-grade content within the approved 20–25% range, and completed independent verification, with zero recurrence of unintended C-grade output attributable to blending.
car.effectivenessEvidence: Pending implementation and monitoring. Review the next 10 applicable batch records, blend test results, verification signoffs, training records, and the 30-day recurrence trend before determining effectiveness.

actions.action: Review recent applicable blend records; identify and contain any other mixed-grade combinations.
Revise the blend/grind instruction and batch record to require grade, lot, and approved ratio verification before charging material.
Add independent verification and signoff before any C-grade material is added to an A-grade blend.
Train affected operators on the revised controls and retain attendance and competency records.
